questions.prompt: The client likes a picture except for one object. What should you do?

options.text: Edit the image: name the object, describe the new one, and keep the rest the same.
options.explanation: Right. This is Google's "change only the ... keep everything else" pattern.

options.text: Generate a brand-new image with the same prompt and hope the room looks similar. It will be like the old one.
options.explanation: A new generation changes many things the client approved.

options.text: Throw the picture away and brief a photographer to shoot the whole scene again.
options.explanation: An edit can solve this much faster.

questions.prompt: What does OpenAI's doc say about mask shapes in GPT Image edits?

options.text: The model uses the mask as guidance but may not follow its exact shape.
options.explanation: Right. Inspect the edges after an edit.

options.text: The model follows the mask to the pixel, so edges never need checking.
options.explanation: The docs say it may not.

options.text: A mask is not needed and not allowed on the edits endpoint at all. Only a text prompt is allowed.
options.explanation: The edits endpoint accepts a mask.

questions.prompt: Which mask file fits an image that is a 1536x1024 PNG?

options.text: A 1536x1024 PNG saved with an alpha channel.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says the mask must match the image's format and size and have an alpha channel.

options.text: A 300x200 JPEG without an alpha channel. Saved at high quality.
options.explanation: It fails the size, format and alpha channel rules.
